aiDescription.summary: This bill amends the Radiation Exposure Compensation Act to add Guam as a covered Pacific test area, add renal disease to compensable illnesses, set specific qualifying presence periods for leukemia and other listed diseases, and include Enewetak Atoll radiological‑cleanup personnel. It applies to individuals physically present in affected Pacific areas during the listed dates (including the 1946–1992 windows and April–November 1962) and to Armed Forces who cleaned up Enewetak (May 1, 1977–May 31, 1980).

description.text: Parity for Pacific Radiation Survivors Act

impact.summary: The bill adds Guam to the Radiation Exposure Compensation Act’s list of Pacific test sites, extends covered exposure dates, and adds Enewetak Atoll radiological‑cleanup participants (May 1, 1977–May 31, 1980). Guam residents and U.S. Armed Forces veterans from that cleanup could file leukemia and specified‑disease claims, now including renal disease, with the Justice Department’s Radiation Exposure Compensation Program.

latestAction.text: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.

bill.title: Parity for Pacific Radiation Survivors Act
